function f mapping nonnegative real numb.analysis: We can model nonnegative reals with the type ℝ≥0 (alias NNReal). The expression sqrt(2 + sqrt(x)) is well-typed in ℝ using Real.sqrt. Given x : ℝ≥0, coercions let us view x : ℝ, so Real.sqrt x ≥ 0, hence 2 + Real.sqrt x ≥ 0, and then Real.sqrt (2 + Real.sqrt x) ≥ 0. Therefore we can package this Real value back into ℝ≥0 using a subtype constructor (or ofReal/toNNReal). Thus f : ℝ≥0 → ℝ≥0 is directly definable.
formal_correspondents: Subtype.mk (⟨_, _⟩) to build an ℝ≥0 from a nonneg ℝ

recursively defined sequence of real num.analysis: Since f maps ℝ≥0 → ℝ≥0, it is natural to take the sequence values in ℝ≥0 (and coerce to ℝ when needed). A standard Lean formalization uses 0-based indexing: define s : ℕ → ℝ≥0 by s 0 = ⟨Real.sqrt 2, Real.sqrt_nonneg 2⟩ and s (n+1) = f (s n). Alternatively, s can be given via iteration: s n = Function.iterate f n (⟨Real.sqrt 2, Real.sqrt_nonneg 2⟩). If one insists on a sequence in ℝ, compose with the coercion ℝ≥0 → ℝ.
formal_correspondents: Nat.rec (primitive recursion) for defining s 0 and s (n+1)
Coercion ℝ≥0 → ℝ if a ℝ-valued sequence is needed

a sequence of real numbers being strictl.analysis: Given s : ℕ → ℝ and c : ℝ, the property 'strictly bounded above by c' is exactly the formula ∀ n : ℕ, s n < c, using the strict order on ℝ. This is a direct predicate with no new definitions required.

sequence of real numbers defined by a_i.analysis: Define a : ℕ → ℝ by a i = Real.sqrt (i + 1) - Real.sqrt i, where the naturals are coerced to reals via the canonical cast. This uses Real.sqrt and subtraction in ℝ.
formal_correspondents: a : ℕ → ℝ defined by fun i => Real.sqrt (i + 1) - Real.sqrt i

two topologies on the same set being com.analysis: Topologies on a fixed type α are TopologicalSpace α, and they form a complete lattice in mathlib. Comparability under inclusion means either t ≤ u or u ≤ t in the order on TopologicalSpace α (this order corresponds to inclusion of open sets). Hence the statement is expressible as t ≤ u ∨ u ≤ t.
formal_correspondents: Disjunction (∨) to express comparability: t ≤ u ∨ u ≤ t

two topologies on the same set being not.analysis: TopologicalSpace α carries a complete lattice structure, with the order t ≤ u meaning: every u-open set is t-open. "Not comparable" means neither t ≤ u nor u ≤ t holds. This is directly expressible as ¬ (t ≤ u) ∧ ¬ (u ≤ t) (or equivalently ¬ (t ≤ u ∨ u ≤ t)). No additional mathematical definitions are required beyond the existing order and logical connectives.
formal_correspondents: LE (≤) instance on TopologicalSpace α (complete lattice)

subbasis for a topology on a set X.analysis: Given a family S : Set (Set X) of subsets, the topology they (sub)generate is TopologicalSpace.GenerateFrom S. One standard way to express that S is a subbasis for a topology t on X is simply t = TopologicalSpace.GenerateFrom S. This uses only existing primitives: sets of sets, equality of topologies, and the generator constructor.
formal_correspondents: (optionally) IsTopologicalBasis for bases, when promoting a subbasis to a basis of finite intersections if needed

lower limit topology ℝ_l on the real lin.analysis: The lower limit (Sorgenfrey) topology can be defined as the topology generated by the family of half-open intervals [a,b) = Ico a b. A concrete definition is τ_ll := TopologicalSpace.GenerateFrom { U | ∃ a b : ℝ, a < b ∧ U = Ico a b }. This uses standard interval constructors and the generator for topologies. If desired one can show this family is a basis via IsTopologicalBasis, but the topology itself is directly definable by GenerateFrom.
formal_correspondents: Ico : ℝ → ℝ → Set ℝ (half-open interval [a,b))
Exists (∃), conjunction (∧), and equality (=) to describe the generating family

K-topology ℝ_K on the real line (topolog.analysis: Define K as the set of reciprocals of positive integers; using positive naturals (PNat) avoids the 1/0 corner case: K := Set.range (fun n : ℕ+ => (1 : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)). Then take the generating family B consisting of (a,b) and (a,b) \ K, i.e., U = Ioo a b or U = Ioo a b \ K for some a < b. The topology is τ_K := TopologicalSpace.GenerateFrom B. This matches the usual presentation of the K-topology as generated by that basis. No new primitives beyond sets, intervals, set difference, and GenerateFrom are required.
formal_correspondents: ℝ, ℕ+, coercions (PNat → ℝ via Nat.cast)
Set.range to define K := {1/n : n ∈ ℕ+}
Ioo : ℝ → ℝ → Set ℝ (open interval (a,b))
Set.diff (\) to form Ioo a b \ K
Logical connectives and ∃ to describe the generating family

topology on ℝ generated by the basis of.analysis: Let B be the set of all open intervals with rational endpoints, B := { U | ∃ a b : ℚ, (a : ℝ) < (b : ℝ) ∧ U = Ioo (a : ℝ) (b : ℝ) }. The topology generated by this basis is τ_Q := TopologicalSpace.GenerateFrom B. This is the standard second-countable base for the Euclidean topology on ℝ, but regardless of identifying it with the usual topology, its definition via GenerateFrom is immediate.
formal_correspondents: ℝ, ℚ with Rat.cast : ℚ → ℝ
Exists (∃), conjunction (∧), equality (=) to specify the generating family

sequence of functions f_n: [0,1] → ℝ def.analysis: The domain [0,1] is modeled as the subtype ↥(Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) = {x : ℝ // 0 ≤ x ∧ x ≤ 1}. A sequence of functions is a function f : ℕ → (↥(Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) → ℝ). Each term is defined by f n x = (Subtype.coe x : ℝ) ^ n using the natural-number power on ℝ. No additional structure is needed.
formal_correspondents: Set.Icc : α → α → Set α (with α = ℝ)
Pow.pow (^) on ℝ with exponent ℕ
f : ℕ → (↥(Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) → ℝ), f n x := (x : ℝ) ^ n

pointwise convergence of a sequence of f.analysis: Pointwise convergence on a subset S ⊆ X can be expressed via filters: for a sequence of functions F : ℕ → (X → ℝ) and a target function g : X → ℝ, we say F converges pointwise on S if ∀ x ∈ S, Tendsto (fun n => F n x) atTop (nhds (g x)). This directly uses Lean's Filter/Tendsto infrastructure; no topology on X is needed (only on the codomain, ℝ).
formal_correspondents: Filter.Tendsto : (α → β) → Filter α → Filter β → Prop
Set X, S : Set X, membership x ∈ S
F : ℕ → (X → ℝ), g : X → ℝ, statement: ∀ x ∈ S, Tendsto (fun n => F n x) atTop (nhds (g x))

pointwise limit function g: [0,1] → ℝ wi.analysis: Model [0,1] as the subtype ↥(Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1). Since 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 holds for all x in the domain, the definition can be given piecewise using a decidable comparison with 1: g x := if (x : ℝ) < 1 then 0 else 1. This yields g(1) = 1 and g(x) = 0 for 0 ≤ x < 1. Alternatively, g can be defined as the indicator of {1} with value 1.
formal_correspondents: Set.Icc : ℝ → ℝ → Set ℝ and the subtype ↥(Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)
Alternative: Set.indicator : Set α → (α → β) → α → β on the set {1} : Set ℝ

limit point of a subset A ⊆ X in a topol.analysis: Given a topological space X, a point x is a limit (accumulation) point of A if every neighborhood of x intersects A \ {x}. This is expressed as ∀ V, V ∈ nhds x → (V ∩ (A \ {x})).Nonempty. Equivalently, x ∈ closure (A \ {x}). Both formulations are directly available via Mathlib's filters and set operations.
formal_correspondents: nhds : X → Filter X; membership V ∈ nhds x
closure : Set X → Set X (equivalent formulation: x ∈ closure (A \ {x}))

limit point compactness (every infinite.analysis: This is a topological property of X: ∀ S : Set X, S.Infinite → ∃ x : X, every neighborhood of x meets S \ {x}. Using the limit-point predicate as in the previous item, the property is expressed as ∀ S, S.Infinite → ∃ x, ∀ V ∈ nhds x, (V ∩ (S \ {x})).Nonempty. An equivalent formulation is ∀ S, S.Infinite → ∃ x, x ∈ closure (S \ {x}). No new primitives are required.
formal_correspondents: nhds : X → Filter X; V ∈ nhds x

nested (decreasing) sequence C_1 ⊇ C_2 ⊇.analysis: A nested sequence is a function C : ℕ → Set X with Antitone C, meaning C (n+1) ⊆ C n for all n. Closedness is IsClosed (C n), and nonemptiness is (C n).Nonempty. All of these are standard in mathlib for an arbitrary topological space X.
formal_correspondents: Antitone C  (or equivalently ∀ n, C (n+1) ⊆ C n)

property that every nested sequence of c.analysis: This is a single proposition quantifying over all sequences C : ℕ → Set X that are decreasing (Antitone C), closed (∀ n, IsClosed (C n)) and nonempty (∀ n, (C n).Nonempty), and asserting that the indexed intersection ⋂ n, C n is nonempty. In Lean, ⋂ n, C n is the iInter of C viewed as sets.

supremum metric on [0,1]^ω given by d(x,.analysis: [0,1]^ω can be modeled as the Pi type α := ℕ → Icc (0 : ℝ) 1. Mathlib equips every Pi type with an EMetricSpace instance by taking the supremum of coordinatewise edist: edist x y = ⨆ n, edist (x n) (y n). Since Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 is a metric space (as a subtype of ℝ), it inherits an EMetricSpace, hence α gets the canonical supremum EMetric via the Pi instance. This is exactly the supremum metric but valued in ℝ≥0∞; here it is always finite (≤ 1), so one can if desired pass to a real-valued distance by dist x y := (edist x y).toReal, yielding the usual sup metric d(x,y) = sup_n |x n − y n|. Even without explicitly re-packaging into a MetricSpace, the function d as described and the built-in EMetric formulation are directly expressible.
formal_correspondents: Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 : Set ℝ and the subtype ↥(Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)
[EMetricSpace α] (Pi instance): edist x y = ⨆ n : ℕ, edist (x n) (y n)
Alternative explicit function: d : α → α → ℝ := fun x y => sSup (Set.range (fun n => Real.abs ((x n : ℝ) - (y n : ℝ))))
Real.abs, HAdd.hSub on ℝ, Set.range, sSup on ℝ (conditionally complete lattice structure)

uniform topology on [0,1]^ω induced by t.analysis: With α := ℕ → Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 equipped with the Pi EMetricSpace (supremum of coordinatewise edist), mathlib provides the associated UniformSpace α via EMetricSpace.toUniformSpace, and its induced topology via UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace. This is the uniform topology induced by the supremum metric. If one explicitly defines a real-valued sup metric (dist = (edist).toReal), Metric.toUniformSpace produces the same uniform topology.
formal_correspondents: (optionally) Metric.toUniformSpace if using a real-valued sup metric dist
